mainTopic: Why רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue about a lost משכון: שמואל's rule, רבי יצחק's rule, or the status of a שומר אבדה.
overview: A ברייתא records an argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא about a lender who lost the משכון, and the גמרא looks for the reason behind it. It first suggests the משכון was worth less than the loan, so they would be arguing about שמואל's rule. It rejects this: in that case everyone disagrees with שמואל. Instead it says the משכון was worth the full loan, and they argue about רבי יצחק's rule, learned from ״וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה״, that a בעל חוב acquires the משכון. The גמרא then asks whether רבי יצחק's rule is really a dispute between תנאים. It answers that רבי יצחק may have spoken only about a משכון taken after the loan, and for that case everyone agrees with him. So the argument must be about a משכון taken at the time of the loan. There the question is the status of a שומר אבדה, and the גמרא begins quoting רבה, who says such a guard is like a שומר חנם. The opposing view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Is the dispute really about שמואל's rule?
steps.stepSummary: If the משכון was worth the whole loan, why would רבי אליעזר let the lender collect? So the גמרא suggests the משכון was worth less, and the two תנאים argue about שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי אליעזר's reason? Isn't it that the משכון was not worth the amount of the loan, and they argue about שמואל's rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the case of the dispute must be. It suggests the משכון was worth less than the loan, so the argument would be about שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משכון was worth the full loan, it is hard to see why רבי אליעזר lets the lender collect after losing it. So the גמרא suggests the משכון was worth less. Then רבי עקיבא would agree with שמואל that the whole loan is lost, and רבי אליעזר would disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Collateral, a pledge the borrower gives the lender
The amount of money (of the loan)
Rather, isn't it that... (introduces a suggested answer)
They argue about

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Eliezer?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו בִּדְלָא שָׁוֵי שִׁיעוּר זוּזֵי
phrases.english: Rather, is it not where it is not worth the amount of the money,
and they disagree about the ruling of Shmuel?
phrases.notes: שמואל said: if he lent a thousand זוז on a mere handle and lost the handle, he loses the whole thousand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו בִּדְלָא שָׁוֵי שִׁיעוּר זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier analysis of the ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue about a lost משכון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case and what principle lie behind the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא?

steps.title: No, the dispute is about רבי יצחק's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. When the משכון is worth less, everyone disagrees with שמואל. The real case is a משכון worth the full loan, and they argue about רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Where it is not worth the loan, everyone disagrees with שמואל. Here it was worth the loan, and they argue about רבי יצחק's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the dispute is about שמואל. It moves the case to a משכון worth the full loan and says the argument is about רבי יצחק. That rule is quoted in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא says both תנאים reject שמואל, so neither cancels a loan larger than the משכון's value. The case is a משכון worth the whole loan. The question is whether the lender owns the משכון and so carries the loss, which is רבי יצחק's idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone (both opinions)
They do not hold of
Where it is worth (the loan)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean שמואל is wrong in practice. It only means that, in this reading, neither רבי אליעזר nor רבי עקיבא holds like him.

phrases.english: No;
where it is not worth the loan,
everyone does not hold of Shmuel's ruling;
and here it is where it is worth the amount of the money,
and they disagree about the opinion of Rabbi Yitzḥak.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; בִּדְלָא שָׁוֵי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לֵית לְהוּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 1 and offers a different case and principle.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the dispute is about שמואל's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: When the משכון is worth less than the loan, both תנאים disagree with שמואל, so that cannot be the point of their argument.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: a lender acquires the משכון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns from the פסוק ״וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה״ that a בעל חוב acquires the משכון. Returning it is only called צדקה if it belongs to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: how do we know a lender acquires a משכון? The פסוק says 'and it shall be צדקה for you.' If he did not acquire it, where is his צדקה? So a lender acquires the משכון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יצחק's rule and shows how he learns it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls returning a poor man's משכון for his use a צדקה, a righteous act. That only makes sense if the lender is giving up something that is his. So the lender counts as owning the משכון, and if it is lost, the loss is his.

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor, the lender
Acquires, becomes the owner of
Righteousness, a righteous act
From where do we know?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק: a בעל חוב acquires the משכון, learned from ״וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה״. At this stage the גמרא says רבי עקיבא holds like him and רבי אליעזר does not. In step 6 the גמרא changes course: everyone accepts רבי יצחק for a משכון taken after the loan.
steps.whyThisMatters: At this stage of the סוגיא, this rule is offered as the reason רבי עקיבא makes the lender lose the value of a lost משכון. Steps 6 and 7 later move the dispute to a different reason, the status of a שומר אבדה.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzḥak says:
From where do we know that a creditor acquires collateral?
As it is stated: “And it shall be a righteousness for you.”
If he does not acquire the collateral,
from where is his righteousness?
phrases.notes: He means: if it isn't his, returning it costs him nothing, so why call it צדקה?

phrases.english: From here we learn that a creditor acquires collateral.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִנַּיִן לְבַעַל חוֹב שֶׁקּוֹנֶה מַשְׁכּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the rule of רבי יצחק that step 2 said the dispute depends on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל חוב acquires the משכון, learned from ״וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה״.

steps.title: Is רבי יצחק's rule a dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא argue about רבי יצחק's rule, then his rule would be argued over by תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבי יצחק's rule is a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question that follows from step 2. If the תנאים argue about רבי יצחק's rule, then רבי אליעזר disagrees with it. The next step responds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's rule is stronger when no תנא disagrees with it. Here the גמרא checks whether רבי יצחק's rule is really rejected by one side of the ברייתא, namely רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say?
It is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Shall we say that the opinion of Rabbi Yitzḥak is a dispute between tanna’im?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a consequence from the answer in steps 2 and 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי אליעזר disagree with רבי יצחק's rule?

steps.title: רבי יצחק may have spoken only about a משכון taken after the loan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on that idea. רבי יצחק may only have meant a משכון taken after the loan. Did he ever say a lender acquires a משכון taken at the time of the loan?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? Say רבי יצחק meant a משכון taken not at the time of the loan. Did he say this about one taken at the time of the loan?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the claim that the dispute is simply about רבי יצחק. His rule may cover only a משכון taken after the loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of ״וּלְךָ תִּהְיֶה צְדָקָה״ speaks about a משכון taken later, when the debt was not paid. A משכון given at the moment of the loan may be different. So the dispute may not be about רבי יצחק's rule at all, since he may never have spoken about that case.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you understand it so? (a rhetorical pushback)
Say that
At the time of the loan
Did he say? (meaning: he did not)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two kinds of משכון here: one taken after the loan, and one taken when the loan was given. רבי יצחק's rule is clear only for the first kind.

phrases.english: And can you understand it that way?!
Say that Rabbi Yitzḥak said it
where he took collateral from him not at the time of the loan;
where he took collateral at the time of the loan, did he say so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea in step 4 by narrowing the scope of רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that the dispute in the ברייתא is simply about רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יצחק's rule may apply only to a משכון taken after the loan, not to one taken when the loan was given.

steps.title: Everyone accepts רבי יצחק for a later משכון, so the dispute is about a משכון taken with the loan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reframes the case. For a משכון taken after the loan, everyone agrees with רבי יצחק. The dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא is about a משכון taken at the time of the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when he took the משכון not at the time of the loan, nobody argues: everyone holds like רבי יצחק. And here, the case is where he took the משכון at the time of the loan.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the pushback in step 5, the גמרא offers a new picture. רבי יצחק's rule is agreed by everyone, and the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא is moved to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed that רבי יצחק may only have been talking about a משכון taken after the loan. So the גמרא now says nobody argues with him at all. The argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא must be about a משכון taken at the time of the loan, where רבי יצחק's rule does not decide the matter. That means their argument needs a new explanation, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the גמרא is replacing the earlier explanation with a new one.
Not at the time of the loan, meaning the משכון was taken later
At the time of the loan
Everyone agrees; literally, 'the whole world does not argue'
They hold, they accept (a certain opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean anyone rejects רבי יצחק. Everyone accepts his rule for a משכון taken later. The dispute was simply moved to a case his rule does not cover.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי יצחק's rule from being an argument between תנאים, which was the problem raised in step 4.

phrases.english: Rather, where he took collateral from him not at the time of the loan,
everyone agrees, and nobody argues,
that they all hold like רבי יצחק.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יצחק's rule from step 3: the lender acquires the משכון.

phrases.english: And here, the case is where he took collateral at the time of the loan,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 5's point and uses it to move the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא to a משכון taken at the time of the loan.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) so that רבי יצחק is not argued over
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argued about רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone accepts רבי יצחק for a משכון taken later. The dispute is about a משכון taken at the time of the loan.

steps.title: The real argument is about the status of someone guarding a lost item
steps.stepSummary: The תנאים argue about the status of a שומר אבדה. The גמרא cites the אמוראים who argue about this, starting with רבה, who says such a guard is like a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they argue about someone guarding a lost item. As it was stated: about someone guarding a lost item, רבה said he is like an unpaid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the real point of the argument, the status of a שומר אבדה, and starts quoting a known dispute about it. Only רבה's side appears here; the other side comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lender holding a משכון taken at the time of the loan is being compared to someone holding a lost item he found. So the question is what kind of guard he is. רבה says a שומר אבדה is like a שומר חנם, who pays less when something goes wrong. This sets up the opposing view, which will show how each תנא fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone guarding a lost item he found until he returns it
They argue about (this point)
An unpaid guard, who does not pay if the item is lost or stolen

phrases.english: and they argue about someone guarding a lost item;
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: as it was stated: someone guarding a lost item,
רבה said: he is like an unpaid guard,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְשׁוֹמֵר אֲבֵדָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי; דְּאִיתְּמַר: שׁוֹמֵר אֲבֵדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 6 moved the dispute to a משכון taken at the time of the loan. This step names the reason for that dispute: the status of a שומר אבדה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the dispute to a known argument between אמוראים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without רבי יצחק's rule, it was unclear what the תנאים argue about.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about whether a שומר אבדה is like a שומר חנם (רבה) or follows the view that comes next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: a שומר אבדה is like a שומר חנם.
